riassunto.titolo_giorno: Hob porta l'AI sui documenti locali e Siri guadagna la memoria con iOS 27.2
riassunto.in_breve: Tra le novità principali di oggi spicca Hob, un software open source che permette di elaborare ed esaminare i propri file sul computer in totale riservatezza. Sul fronte degli assistenti diffusi, Apple aggiorna Siri AI introducendo la memoria del contesto, mentre OpenAI lancia dots per organizzare gli impegni in background.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Un assistente personale integrato nelle app desktop e mobile di ChatGPT che lavora in background collegandosi a calendario, email e computer.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Pianificare impegni e gestire compiti quotidiani lasciando che l'assistente lavori autonomamente in background.

da_provare.a_cosa_serve: Un'applicazione per computer che permette di elaborare ed esaminare i propri file e documenti in locale usando modelli AI che funzionano direttamente sul dispositivo.
da_provare.come_sfruttarla: Analizzare contratti, appunti e documenti di lavoro riservati senza caricare alcun dato online.

gemme.a_cosa_serve: Piattaforma open source per il tracciamento GPS in tempo reale di veicoli o smartphone tramite interfaccia web.
gemme.perche_gemma: È gratuita, open source e installabile sul proprio server per la massima riservatezza sui dati di spostamento.
gemme.con_ai: Si può integrare con strumenti AI per analizzare i percorsi storici e ottimizzare gli spostamenti.

gemme.a_cosa_serve: Sistema open source per registrare il cielo notturno in 4K e catalogare automaticamente il passaggio di meteore.
gemme.perche_gemma: Salva tutti i filmati direttamente sul proprio disco locale senza dipendere da servizi cloud esterni.
gemme.con_ai: Utilizza modelli AI per analizzare i fotogrammi e individuare le scie luminose senza dover controllare manualmente ore di video.

notizie.titolo: Con iOS 27.2 arrivano la memoria delle conversazioni e l'accesso ai messaggi vocali
notizie.riassunto: Con l'aggiornamento a iOS e macOS 27.2, Siri può ricordare le conversazioni passate e consultare allegati e messaggi vocali. Viene aggiunta una funzione per escludere specifiche app dall'accesso dell'assistente e il supporto a 5 nuove lingue.
notizie.come_provarla: Aggiornando il sistema operativo del proprio dispositivo Apple nelle regioni in cui il servizio è supportato.

a116.titolo: Apple releases iOS and macOS 27.2 with new Siri AI features, new Music logo
a116.testo: Today, Apple rolled out the 27.2 updates for its operating systems, including iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and so on. Let’s start with iOS 27.2. This update is heavily focused on Siri AI. It adds a memory feature to Siri, so it can “recall your past conversations” and reference them when chatting with you. It also expands what data sources Siri can access when giving responses to include voicemails, Messages attachments, and more. On the flip side, there is now an “Excluded Apps” option that allows you to “choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access.” Further, Siri AI is now available in five more languages beyond English, as previously announced: French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish—though Siri AI remains unavailable in Europe (and mainland China). Other additions include context-aware suggestions within Messages (like turning a message inviting you to something into a calendar entry), SynthID watermarking support in Photos, and support for user profiles in the Apple TV app. There’s also the new Apple Music branding, plus the arrival of previously promised Apple Pencil support on the iPhone Duo foldable. The macOS Golden Gate 27.2 offers some of the same things: contextual memory for Siri, the same additional Siri AI languages, and miscellaneous unspecified bug fixes. The same goes for the Apple Watch—again, mostly the same Siri-related updates. visionOS 27.2 includes the new languages and updated Music icon, as well. a110.titolo: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
a110.testo: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots, its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done. Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding.
